scope: Primary-source regulatory and mechanism review for a research candidate library; US approved indications summarized, not prescribing guidance.
interpretation_rules: Approval in an oncology or pulmonary indication does not establish efficacy, hepatoprotection, or acceptable benefit-risk for liver fibrosis.
PDGFRA/FLT4 explicit flags describe the wording in the cited source, not a complete selectivity profile; absence from a label is not evidence of inactivity.
VEGFR3 is the protein name corresponding to FLT4. PDGFR-alpha corresponds to PDGFRA. FLT3 must not be confused with FLT4.
Hepatic warnings and hepatic-impairment dosing restrictions are distinct; a label without a dedicated hepatotoxicity warning does not establish comparative hepatic safety.
DailyMed update dates are record update dates; prescribing-information revision dates can differ.
Candidate compounds are inhibitors unless otherwise stated. Binding predictions alone cannot determine therapeutic direction or justify systemic kinase inhibition.

compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases with a progressive phenotype; slowing pulmonary-function decline in systemic-sclerosis-associated ILD.
compounds.target_mechanism: ATP-competitive multikinase inhibitor: PDGFR-alpha/beta, FGFR1-3, VEGFR1-3, CSF1R and FLT3; also Lck, Lyn and Src.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Dedicated warning for elevated liver enzymes and DILI, including fatal postmarketing liver injury. Liver testing before treatment, regularly in the first 3 months and subsequently. Reduced dose in mild hepatic impairment; not recommended in moderate/severe impairment.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Pulmonary antifibrotic approval is not liver-fibrosis approval; the label documents clinically important hepatic risk.

compounds.approved_indications_summary: Defined settings of Ph-positive CML/ALL; PDGFR-rearranged MDS/MPD; aggressive systemic mastocytosis without KIT D816V or unknown status; HES/CEL; DFSP; KIT-positive unresectable/metastatic GIST and adjuvant KIT-positive GIST.
compounds.target_mechanism: BCR-ABL, PDGF receptor and KIT inhibitor. Mechanism section names the PDGF receptor family; the HES/CEL indication explicitly identifies FIP1L1-PDGFR-alpha fusion kinase.
compounds.pdgfra_explicit_qualification: Alpha is explicit in indication 1.7; mechanism 12.1 uses generic PDGF receptor wording.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Dedicated hepatotoxicity warning: fatal liver failure and severe injury requiring transplantation reported. Monitor liver function before therapy and monthly or as indicated; interruption/dose reduction may be necessary.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Do not imply inhibition of every PDGFRA mutant; indication-specific biology and hepatic toxicity prevent blanket liver-repurposing claims.

compounds.regulatory_status: Investigational. Sponsor's indexed primary page states no regulatory authority approval; no approved FDA label identified.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: None established; studied in FLT3-mutant AML and PDGFRA-mutant GIST.
compounds.target_mechanism: Primary biochemical/cellular work supports PDGFRA and PDGFRB inhibition, including PDGFRA D842V, and FLT3 inhibition. FLT3 activity is not FLT4 evidence.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: No approved label to classify. The 44-patient chemotherapy-combination AML study reported dose reductions for adverse events including liver dysfunction; attribution cannot isolate crenolanib from chemotherapy. Human liver-fibrosis safety is unestablished.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Use as an investigational mechanistic comparator; do not call clinically validated or hepatoprotective.
compounds.clinical_evidence: Wang et al., J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1776-1787, DOI 10.1200/JCO.23.01061, NCT02283177: 44 adults receiving crenolanib plus intensive chemotherapy. PDGFRA-mutant GIST phase II registered as NCT01243346.

compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with unresectable/metastatic GIST carrying PDGFRA exon 18 mutations, including D842V; advanced systemic mastocytosis; indolent systemic mastocytosis.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits KIT D816V, PDGFRA and PDGFRA D842 mutants and additional KIT mutants; potential targets include wild-type KIT, PDGFRB and CSF1R.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: No dedicated hepatotoxicity warning in the reviewed warnings section; increased bilirubin, AST and ALT occur in laboratory adverse-event tables. Dose reduction is recommended in severe hepatic impairment.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Mutation-oriented oncology/mastocytosis evidence does not establish benefit or safety for wild-type PDGFRA inhibition in liver fibrosis.

compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with advanced GIST following at least 3 prior kinase inhibitors, including imatinib.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits wild-type and mutant KIT and PDGFRA; other in-vitro targets include PDGFRB, TIE2, VEGFR2 and BRAF.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: No dedicated hepatotoxicity warning in the reviewed warnings section. INVICTUS laboratory abnormalities included increased bilirubin and ALT. Current section 8.6 recommends no dose adjustment for Child-Pugh A, B or C.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: No-dose-adjustment guidance is pharmacokinetic/label guidance, not proof of hepatic safety or liver-fibrosis efficacy.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2012; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Advanced renal cell carcinoma: first line with avelumab or pembrolizumab; monotherapy after one prior systemic therapy fails.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR1, VEGFR2 and VEGFR3 at therapeutic plasma concentrations; PDGFRA is not named in section 12.1.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Section 5.11 warns of liver-enzyme elevations with monotherapy and increased frequency of grade 3–4 ALT/AST elevations with avelumab or pembrolizumab. Liver tests require monitoring; severe combination-associated hepatotoxicity can require interruption, corticosteroids or permanent discontinuation. No hepatic boxed warning.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Cancer approval and kinase inhibition do not establish efficacy or safety for liver fibrosis; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2021; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with relapsed or refractory advanced renal cell carcinoma after at least two systemic therapies.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR1/2/3 phosphorylation, c-KIT and PDGFR-beta at clinically relevant concentrations; PDGFRA is not named.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: No dedicated hepatotoxicity warning or boxed warning in this label. TIVO-3 laboratory abnormalities include ALT elevation (30%; grade 3–4, 4%), AST elevation (28%; grade 3–4, 1%), and bilirubin elevation (11%; grade 3–4, 3%). Dose adjustment applies to moderate hepatic impairment; severe impairment is to be avoided.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Absence of a dedicated warning is not evidence of hepatic safety; no liver-fibrosis indication or efficacy is established by this label.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2015; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Progressive, recurrent/metastatic radioactive-iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer; advanced renal cell carcinoma with pembrolizumab first line or everolimus after one antiangiogenic therapy; unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma first line; advanced pMMR/non-MSI-H endometrial carcinoma with pembrolizumab after systemic therapy progression when curative surgery/radiation is unsuitable.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits VEGFR1/2/3; label explicitly identifies VEGFR3 as FLT4 and includes PDGFRA, FGFR1–4, KIT and RET.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Section 5.4 hepatotoxicity warning includes serious and fatal hepatic events. Liver monitoring is required; grade 3–4 toxicity may require withholding/discontinuation and hepatic failure requires discontinuation. No hepatic boxed warning.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Hepatocellular carcinoma approval does not establish antifibrotic efficacy or suitability for nonmalignant liver disease; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2006; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adult GIST after imatinib progression/intolerance; advanced renal cell carcinoma; adjuvant therapy after nephrectomy for high-risk recurrent RCC; progressive, well-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors with unresectable locally advanced/metastatic disease.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits PDGFR-alpha/beta, VEGFR1/2/3, KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R and RET.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed hepatotoxicity warning: hepatic injury can be severe or fatal. Hepatic monitoring and interruption, dose reduction or discontinuation are specified; section 5.1 describes liver failure/death.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Oncology approval and receptor inhibition do not establish antifibrotic benefit or acceptable safety in liver fibrosis; no such indication is listed.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2009; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with advanced renal cell carcinoma or advanced soft-tissue sarcoma after prior chemotherapy. Efficacy in adipocytic sarcoma or GIST is not established.
compounds.target_mechanism: Multikinase inhibitor including VEGFR1/2/3, PDGFR-alpha/beta, FGFR1/3, KIT, ITK, LCK and c-FMS.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed hepatotoxicity warning for severe and fatal hepatic toxicity. Baseline and ongoing liver monitoring and withholding, dose reduction or discontinuation according to severity are required.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Oncology approval and receptor inhibition do not establish antifibrotic efficacy; hepatic toxicity is particularly relevant to repurposing for liver disease. No liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2005; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma; advanced renal cell carcinoma; progressive, locally recurrent/metastatic differentiated thyroid carcinoma refractory to radioactive iodine.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits RAF-family and cell-surface kinases including VEGFR1/2/3, KIT, FLT3, RET and PDGFR-beta. PDGFRA is not named.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Section 5.10 warns of drug-induced hepatocellular injury, potentially causing liver failure or death; severe injury occurred in 2/3357 patients in a global monotherapy database. Regular liver tests and discontinuation for significant unexplained transaminase elevations are specified. No hepatic boxed warning.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Hepatocellular carcinoma approval does not establish antifibrotic efficacy or safety for nonmalignant liver disease; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2012; DailyMed marketing status New Drug Application.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer (fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin/irinotecan, anti-VEGF and, if RAS wild-type, anti-EGFR therapy); advanced unresectable/metastatic GIST after imatinib and sunitinib; hepatocellular carcinoma after sorafenib.
compounds.target_mechanism: Regorafenib and/or active metabolites inhibit multiple kinases, explicitly including VEGFR3 and PDGFR-alpha, at clinically achieved concentrations.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed hepatotoxicity warning for severe and sometimes fatal hepatic toxicity. Baseline and ongoing liver monitoring plus interruption, reduction or discontinuation according to severity/persistence are specified. Hepatic warning updated February 2026.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Hepatocellular carcinoma approval does not establish antifibrotic efficacy or safety for nonmalignant liver disease; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed.

compounds.regulatory_status: US approved; initial approval 2012. Newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL combination indication has accelerated approval.
compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults: newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL with chemotherapy; Ph+ ALL monotherapy when other kinase inhibitors are unsuitable or T315I-positive; CP-CML after resistance/intolerance to at least two kinase inhibitors; AP/BP-CML when other kinase inhibitors are unsuitable; T315I-positive CML. Not recommended for newly diagnosed CP-CML.
compounds.target_mechanism: Inhibits ABL and T315I-mutant ABL. Label names VEGFR/PDGFR families among additional targets but does not specify VEGFR3/FLT4 or PDGFRA isoforms.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Boxed warning includes hepatotoxicity, liver failure and death, alongside arterial/venous vascular events and heart failure. Liver-test monitoring and interruption or discontinuation according to severity are specified.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Family-level label target information cannot independently establish binding to either requested isoform; no liver-fibrosis indication is listed, and oncology approval does not establish antifibrotic benefit.

compounds.regulatory_status: Nonclinical research compound; no approved medicine label identified.
compounds.target_mechanism: Indolinone inhibitor of VEGFR3 kinase/ligand-induced phosphorylation in recombinant and cellular assays. The original study reported strong VEGFR3 inhibition at 5 micromolar with little/no VEGFR2 effect; at 50 micromolar VEGFR2 inhibition also occurred. Possible inhibition of other RTKs was explicitly acknowledged.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: No clinical label or established human hepatic-safety profile. Nonclinical experimental use must not be described as clinically safe.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: A VEGFR3 inhibition control for mechanistic experiments; cannot substitute for VEGFR3 activation or validate the therapeutic direction of FLT4 modulation.

source_refs.sections: Kirkin et al., Eur J Biochem 2001;268:5530-5540, Figures 6-7 and Discussion

compounds.target_mechanism: The label states that its mechanism in IPF has not been established. It is not label-established as a direct PDGFRA or FLT4 inhibitor.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: Dedicated warning for elevated liver enzymes/DILI, including fatal postmarketing liver injury. Liver tests before therapy, monthly for 6 months and every 3 months thereafter. Not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Suitable as an approved pulmonary antifibrotic comparator; target-specific docking relevance is unestablished and pulmonary approval is not hepatoprotection.

chemical_identity_note.label_section_11: One chiral center; R-stereoisomer. Label name contains (5R) and the displayed structure specifies sulfoxide sulfur stereochemistry.

compounds.approved_indications_summary: Adults with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and progressive pulmonary fibrosis.
compounds.target_mechanism: PDE4 inhibitor with at least nine-fold in-vitro preference for PDE4B over PDE4A/C/D; elevates intracellular cAMP. Not label-established as a PDGFRA or FLT4 inhibitor.
compounds.hepatic_safety_summary: No dedicated hepatotoxicity warning in reviewed label. Severe hepatic impairment has not been studied and use is not recommended; mild/moderate impairment uses the standard dose.
compounds.liver_fibrosis_evidence_caution: Approved pulmonary antifibrotic comparator with a different molecular target. Absence of a dedicated liver warning is not comparative proof of hepatic safety.
